description: The Estonian Rescue Board, Päästeamet, publishes detailed statistics on the events its fire and rescue services attend. Yearly Excel tables give rescue events by type and county and by type and month for 2010 to 2020, with a change of counting method in 2015. A municipal statistics page shows events by county, municipality, event type and month from 2013 onwards and lets users export all data or a filtered selection as CSV; it is updated daily, so the current year runs to the previous day. Further pages cover fires, building fires, water accidents, the rescue station network and volunteer rescuers, and some data are also in the national open data portal. The data are free and available to download from the Rescue Board site; no licence is stated on the statistics pages. Caveats: the 2015 method change breaks the series, and the municipal page is interactive, so the CSV is the stable route. Simulation uses: modelling demand on fire and rescue stations by municipality, testing station closures or mergers, and relating storm and flood events to rescue workload. Related records: the Nordic fire statistics (data-nordic-fire-statistics) include Estonia in a regional comparison, and the CTIF world fire statistics (data-ctif-world-fire-statistics) give international totals.
